pr_body:
## Description
There's a possibility of a race codition on CApplicationPlayerCallback::m_itemCurrentFile leading to heap-use-after-free reported by the address sanitizer [1].
    
The crash happens when GUI_MSG_UPDATE_ITEM is being handled. CApplicationPlayerCallback::m_itemCurrentFile can be accessed concurrently by the main thread in CApplication::OnMessage and CApplicationPlayerCallback::OnPlayBackStarted in the video thread.

Sometimes CApplicationPlayerCallback::OnPlayBackStarted is called first, resets the m_itemCurrentFile (and deallocates the object). Then CApplication::OnMessage tries to read it - this is where heap-use-after-free occurs.
    
In order to mitigate the issue introduce additional messages GUI_MSG_PLAYBACK_PAUSED, GUI_MSG_PLAYBACK_RESUMED, GUI_MSG_PLAYBACK_PAUSED and GUI_MSG_PLAYBACK_SPEED_CHANGED. Those messages are sent from the GUI thread to the main thread. That way the access to CApplicationPlayerCallback::m_itemCurrentFile is serialized (it will be accessed only from the main thread).

## Motivation and context
It fixes https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/issues/23247.

## How has this been tested?
Mainly it has been tested on Arch Linux ARM on 20.1. Since 4 months Kodi haven't crashed. Previously it was crashing couple of times a month.

## What is the effect on users?
Kodi shouldn't crash while switching the items.

issue_context.title: Heap-use-after-free in CFileItem::UpdateInfo due to race condition on CApplicationPlayerCallback::m_itemCurrentFile
issue_context.body:
## Bug report
### Describe the bug
There's a race condition on `CApplicationPlayerCallback::m_itemCurrentFile` between two threads. The first thread is the main Kodi thread (where `CApplication::OnMessage` is called), and the second thread is the video player thread (where `CApplicationPlayerCallback::OnPlayBackStarted` is called).

I've confirmed that `m_itemCurrentFile` is accessed from two different contexts by adding following logs:
https://github.com/dobo90/xbmc/commit/d0e4dcf50b1c579443ae86b4242e9542ba5e0201

The crash happens when `GUI_MSG_UPDATE_ITEM` is being handled. `CApplicationPlayerCallback::m_itemCurrentFile` can be accessed concurrently by the main thread in `CApplication::OnMessage` and `CApplicationPlayerCallback::OnPlayBackStarted` in video thread. Sometimes `CApplicationPlayerCallback::OnPlayBackStarted` is called first, resets the `m_itemCurrentFile` (and deallocates the object) and later `CApplication::OnMessage`  tries to access it - this is where crash happens. It's shown in [address sanitizer report](https://paste.kodi.tv/gexokutajo.kodi).



## Expected Behavior
Kodi doesn't crash.



## Actual Behavior
Kodi randomly crashes after switching the live TV channel. On my Raspberry Pi 4 it crashes few times a month (it's a rare crash).



## Possible Fix
A possible fix is implemented inside [that branch](https://github.com/dobo90/xbmc/commits/20.1-Nexus_cfileitem_heap_after_free_fix). I've introduced `GUI_MSG_PLAYBACK_PAUSED`, `GUI_MSG_PLAYBACK_RESUMED`, `GUI_MSG_PLAYBACK_SEEKED` and `GUI_MSG_PLAYBACK_SPEED_CHANGED` messages to make sure that `CApplicationPlayerCallback::m_itemCurrentFile` is accessed only from one context. To be honest I'm not sure whether it's the best solution that's why I'm creating a problem report instead of a pull request.

If the fix is accepted I can open a PR to master branch, split it into the several commits (as it needed to change type from int to int64_t in `CGUIMessage::{Param1,Param2}`. 


### To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Compile Kodi with address sanitizer enabled (additional options pased to cmake: -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DECM_ENABLE_SANITIZERS=address -DENABLE_DEBUGFISSION=FALSE).
2. Prepare some list of TV channels separated into groups (on my side I use IPTV Simple PVR plugin).
3. Run [that script](https://paste.kodi.tv/kagohepema) which randomly switches the TV channels. I've reproduced it twice on my side: for the first time I needed 15 minutes, for the second time about half an hour.


### Debuglog
The debuglog can be found here (it's the address sanitizer report - Kodi debug logs are too big to paste):
https://paste.kodi.tv/gexokutajo.kodi

### Your Environment
Used Operating system:
 - [ ] Android
 - [ ] iOS
 - [ ] tvOS
 - [X] Linux
 - [ ] macOS
 - [ ] Windows
 - [ ] Windows UWP

 - Operating system version/name: Arch Linux (and Arch Linux ARM on Raspberry Pi 4)
 - Kodi version: 20.1


<!--- End of this issue -->
*note: Once the issue is made we require you to update it with new information or Kodi versions should that be required.
Team Kodi will consider your problem report however, we will not make any promises the problem will be solved.*

review_comments: Please add stdint.h inclusion to the header
I doubt this needs to be an int64_t, would a uint32_t be enough?

Video player uses int64_t for both values:
https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/d3f1d4b10afcff29d4cf49a8f44a49cb24710071/xbmc/cores/VideoPlayer/VideoPlayer.cpp#L3192C2-L3192C2
https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/d3f1d4b10afcff29d4cf49a8f44a49cb24710071/xbmc/cores/VideoPlayer/VideoPlayer.cpp#L3217C1-L3217C1

I'm all for changing to int64_t, but this will cause a *lot* of warnings anywhere GetParamX() is currently used in a calculation and assigned to an int. A change to int64_t should probably come with the brush of a fine-toothed comb.

Approach 1 looks better (though I would call it `GetParam1AsI64()`).

Approach 2 is certainly creative but let's not extend the use of raw pointers.

Overall the "param1/param2" think is a bit hacky. We could add "param3" and "param4" for 64bit ints but that just makes the problem worse.

I'm fine with Approach 1 but I'm open to other ideas that are less hacky.
I've updated the PR. Now it implements Approach 1.
